claims.text: Lattice distortion, grain-boundary sliding, and diffusion-mediated processes explain the elevated-temperature stress–strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Lattice distortion, grain-boundary sliding, and diffusion-mediated processes explain the thermal expansion of HfNbTaTiZr.
Lattice distortion, grain-boundary sliding, and diffusion-mediated processes explain the elevated-temperature elastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Alloy composition and microstructure influence lattice distortion.
Alloy composition and microstructure influence grain-boundary sliding.
Alloy composition and microstructure influence diffusion-mediated processes.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit unusual elastic behavior relative to conventional metallic materials.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit unusual plastic-deformation behavior relative to conventional BCC alloys.
HfNbTaTiZr will be elastically isotropic at room temperature.
HfNbTaTiZr will lack strongly temperature-dependent elastic-anisotropic deformation at elevated temperatures.
The proposed behavior should hold above approximately 500 °C (773 K).
In-situ neutron diffraction can measure lattice-strain evolution and derive single-crystal and macroscopic elastic moduli at elevated temperatures.
Combined neutron diffraction and HRTEM can identify deformation mechanisms in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The exact relationships among composition, microstructure, and elevated-temperature properties remain insufficiently understood.

contradictions.description: The initial state permits a single crystal, while grain-boundary sliding is proposed without qualification as a mediator; a single crystal has no internal grain boundaries on which that mechanism could operate.
